Getting a Dental Implant

A 1-minute patient guide with narration. Press space to pause.

Patient guide

Getting a dental implant.

Here is what to expect, start to finish.

When a tooth is missing.

An implant replaces both the root and the visible tooth, so it looks, feels, and works like a natural tooth.

You'll be comfortable.

We numb the area first. You will feel pressure, but you should not feel pain.

A new root.

A small titanium post is placed in the jawbone, right where the old root used to be.

Time to heal.

Over the next few months, the bone grows around the post and locks it firmly in place.

A connector is added.

A small piece called an abutment is attached to the post. It will hold your new tooth.

Your new tooth.

A custom crown, made to match your other teeth, is attached to the abutment.

Care for it like your own.

Keep the gums around your implant healthy with good daily habits.

Brush twice a dayFloss around the implantKeep your checkups

Questions? Just ask.

Your dental team is happy to walk you through every step before, during, and after your visit.
